review.summary: Independent review of submission sub-mv15wpmr-015f7530 (brief.md only). The brief is well structured: all 45 required ids are present with test-suite tags, the trust boundaries are explicit, each major choice is weighed against an alternative, and the risk register has owners. Seven major findings block approval. (1) The fixture does not pin inventory. My brute force (ev:ev-mv16ez5r-01e792ff) shows that RS-06/09/10/11 hold only when A, B and E each have exactly one bundle on hand. With A at 2 bundles, the planner the brief adopts returns A x2 = 7000 cents with 1 pickup. (2) The honest-status model has no provider PENDING outcome and no derivation rule for the aggregate rescue status. (3) Execute has no stated exclusive claim. Nothing guards against reservation expiry during execute, and outstanding authorizations are never voided on supersession, refusal, authorization failure or cancel. (4) RS-34 narrows the goal's labelling scope. (5) NFR1 cannot be met as written: node:sqlite needs a flag on Node 22.5-22.12 and the browser suites have no script. (6) RS-31/32 replace the PayPal approval with the fake adapter page. (19) The architecture section delegates modules, data model, planner and saga to the unsubmitted docs/build/plan.md, and the fixture table exists only in docs/build/goal.md. Minor and info findings follow. The previous unrecorded draft was checked claim by claim. Its 18 findings were substantiated and kept, with ARCH-8 downgraded to info and ARCH-16 raised to minor. ARCH-19 to ARCH-21 are new.

findings.title: RS-FIX-1 does not pin inventory, so RS-06/09/10/11 hold only under an unstated one-bundle assumption
findings.detail: The brief adopts plan.md section 5 unchanged. That planner enumerates multiplicities 0..ceil(N/qty) per offer, bounded by availability = on_hand - reserved. Neither the brief nor goal.md's RS-FIX-1 table gives on_hand per supplier. In the brief, on_hand occurs only in RS-14 and RISK-4 (ev:ev-mv16g60f-0190c7f8). My brute-force lexicographic solver over the fixture (ev:ev-mv16ez5r-01e792ff) reproduces every expected outcome with one bundle per supplier: A+B 8400 / 2 pickups / 10:30; without B, A+E 9500; without B at 9000, no plan; max 1 pickup, no plan. With A at 2 bundles it returns A x2 = 7000 cents, 1 pickup, which also makes max-pickups-1 feasible. With B at 2 it returns B x2 = 8000. With E at 2, max-pickups-1 becomes feasible at E x2 = 10000. Of all 27 inventories (A, B, E in 0..2), only A=1, B=1, E=1 satisfies RS-06, RS-09, RS-10 and RS-11 together. The oracle property test (<= 6 offers) as described also does not require catalogs with multiplicity > 1.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the brief states the fixture inventory: on_hand = 1 bundle for each of A-E, or offers declared as single-unit 'take it or leave it' lots. RS-06/09/10/11 and RS-14's 'last bundle' must reference it, the seed must load it, and the oracle property test must include catalogs with on_hand >= 2 so that multiplicity is exercised.

findings.title: Honest statuses incomplete: no provider PENDING outcome and no derivation rule for the aggregate rescue status
findings.detail: (a) The project's own integration research (ev:ev-mv16gcdz-01d03c53, marked 'verify'; paypal.com is blocked here, so not re-checked) lists authorization status PENDING and capture status PENDING as provider outcomes. The brief's payment machine (RS-22, RS-25, Workflows 4 and 6) has no such state. A pending capture would have to be shown as captured (false), failed (false) or unknown. But unknown is reserved for lost responses, and the reconciler would then 'resolve' it to a provider state that is still pending. (b) goal.md defines the rescue aggregate, including cancelling, refunding and failed_needs_attention, as derived and never stored. The brief contains none of those three state names (ev:ev-mv16g60f-0190c7f8). RS-36's AC only checks that no stored column exists. An implementation that reports purchase_confirmed while a supplier order is refused, or a refund is pending, would therefore pass.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the brief does all three of the following. (a) Adds explicit pending states (e.g. authorization_pending, capture_pending) with their allowed transitions and reconciler polling, plus the rule that capture never starts from authorization_pending and handover stays blocked while capture_pending; RS-22/RS-25 must name these states. (b) Includes a derivation table from the plan/reservation/payment/fulfilment states to every goal aggregate state, with precedence. (c) Extends RS-36's AC with at least three derivation assertions: any refund_requested/refund_pending gives refunding; a refusal or non_executable with outstanding money gives cancelling or failed_needs_attention as defined; collected only when every supplier order is collected and every capture is completed.

findings.title: Execute lacks an exclusive claim, nothing guards against reservation expiry during capture, and authorizations are never voided outside the capture-failure path
findings.detail: (a) RS-20 relies on 'operation key unique', but the brief never says how the capture operation key is derived. If it is generated per request, two concurrent execute calls (or two processes, which RS-14 already assumes exist) can both pass revalidation and both capture. The PayPal-Request-Id backstop has unverified retention (ev:ev-mv16gcdz-01d03c53), and the fake adapter does not model it. (b) Workflow 6 revalidates 'reservation active' and then captures sequentially. Nothing stops the expiry job from releasing the reservation in between, which would leave a capture against released stock. (c) Void appears only in the capture-phase compensation (Workflow 6, RS-22). The brief does not say what happens to outstanding authorizations, or what the buyer sees, in five cases: RS-21 (one authorization failed, the others stay open), RS-17 (supplier refusal after authorization), RS-13 (plan superseded after authorization at the old amount), reservation expiry, and RS-18 (one supplier's approval cancelled while another is already authorized). RS-13 also does not say when supersession stops applying (after supplier commitment, after capture).
findings.recommendation: Resolved when Workflow 6 and the ACs state four things. (1) The claim mechanism: a deterministic capture operation_key per (supplier order, kind) inserted inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE as the claim, or a plan approved -> executing transition, with RS-20 extended to two OS processes. (2) The reservation is moved to consumed (or marked in-flight) in the same transaction, before the first capture call, with an AC that an expiry pass during execute is a no-op. (3) For RS-13, RS-17, RS-18, RS-21 and expiry: all outstanding authorizations are voided, end in status voided, and the buyer sees a stated next step, with assertions added to those ACs. (4) The point after which a price change no longer supersedes the plan.

findings.title: RS-34 narrows the goal's labelling requirement to fake adapters only
findings.detail: goal.md: 'All demonstration data, simulations, test providers and Sandbox transactions are labelled in the UI and the API'. The brief's RS-34 and its AC cover only payloads and UI from fake adapters (ev:ev-mv16g60f-0190c7f8). Real Sandbox payments and the seeded suppliers A-E with their 'test prices, not market prices' (the phrase does not occur in the brief) are left unlabelled. This weakens a mandatory scope statement, although the brief says requirements are kept unweakened.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when RS-34 and its AC also require three things, tested [D; B] for both adapters: real-adapter payment payloads and UI carry a provider marker (e.g. provider: 'paypal-sandbox') and a visible 'Sandbox - no real money' badge; seeded suppliers, offers and prices carry a demonstration flag that the UI renders; and the 'test prices, not market prices' notice is shown.

findings.title: NFR1 cannot be met as written: node:sqlite is flagged on Node 22.5-22.12, and the browser suites have no script
findings.detail: (a) nodejs.org/api/sqlite.html (checked 2026-10-09) gives the module history: node:sqlite was added in v22.5.0 behind --experimental-sqlite and unflagged in v22.13.0/v23.4.0. The DatabaseSync timeout option arrived in v22.16.0. So a clean clone on Node 22.5-22.12 that runs plain `node` cannot load the database. The brief's Constraints only record Node 22.22 here. ev:ev-mv16frja-017d17a4 shows the flag is still accepted on 22.22, so passing it in scripts is safe. (b) The [B] Playwright suites (RS-17, RS-31..35, NFR2) are assigned to no script. NFR3 lists only npm test and the two live scripts (ev:ev-mv16g60f-0190c7f8). If [B] runs under npm test, a clean clone must download Chromium from Playwright's CDN, which is network beyond npm. The brief notes that Chromium is pre-installed only in this build environment.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the brief does two things. First, it states how node:sqlite loads on every supported version: either npm scripts and the README start command pass --experimental-sqlite (and set the busy timeout via PRAGMA, since the constructor option needs 22.16), or the user approves raising the floor to Node >= 22.13. Second, it defines the script layout: npm test = deterministic node --test only, offline after npm install; npm run test:browser = Playwright, with the one-time browser install documented in the README. NFR1's AC must be phrased against npm test, and the [B] ACs must name test:browser.

findings.title: RS-31/RS-32 replace the user's 'PayPal approvals' with the fake adapter page instead of marking the live variant Unverified
findings.detail: goal.md RS-31: 'Request -> review -> plan -> reservation -> PayPal approvals -> ...'. Its preamble says requirement text is not weakened, and that criteria needing an unreachable integration are marked Unverified with the blocker. The brief's RS-31 reads 'PayPal approvals (fake adapter page)' [B] only (ev:ev-mv16g60f-0190c7f8). RS-32 likewise names only [B]. The Success Criteria extend Sandbox evidence only to RS-18..26. The end-to-end journey through PayPal's hosted Sandbox approval page is the central demonstration for a PayPal hackathon. It is also the only path that would reveal the cross-site return problem in ARCH-10.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when RS-31 and RS-32 each carry two variants. The first is [B fake], deterministic here. The second is [LP, user-run]: through the real Sandbox hosted approval page, with screenshots, recorded as Unverified with blocker A6/Q2 until the user runs it. The Success Criteria must also state that the demo video uses the Sandbox approval page.

findings.title: RS-10's example suggestions include a relaxation that does not yield a plan
findings.detail: For the scenario without B at budget 9000, the brute force (ev:ev-mv16ez5r-01e792ff) gives these results. Budget raised to 9500: A+E at 9500. Deadline moved to 11:20: D alone at 8000. Max pickups 3 or 5: still no plan. A planner that emits 'more pickups' would pass the AC while giving the buyer wrong advice.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when suggestions are defined as computed relaxations, each naming the relaxed constraint and the plan and total it yields (budget 9500 -> A+E; deadline 11:20 -> D at 8000). RS-10 must assert those two values and drop 'more pickups' from its example list.

findings.title: NFR1..4 alias for RS-NF-1..4 is forced by the engine; keep the mapping visible downstream
findings.detail: lib/gates.js:197 defines CRITERION_ID = /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*-?\d+$/. That pattern accepts RS-01 and NFR1 and rejects RS-NF-1 (ev:ev-mv16ggcp-011ee455), so the alias is necessary. The texts are semantically unchanged and the user's ids are kept in parentheses.
findings.recommendation: Add the NFR1..4 = RS-NF-1..4 mapping to docs/build/evidence.md and the acceptance-report template.

findings.title: NFR5/NFR6 requirement text promises more than the ACs test; NFR5's random catalog is undefined
findings.detail: The NFR5 requirement includes 'API p95 < 300 ms'. The NFR6 requirement includes 'logs never contain secrets or raw card/PayPal payloads beyond ids' and 'haiku by default'. Neither AC includes these clauses. NFR5's 'random catalogs <= 12 offers' gives no bounds on bundle sizes or quantities. With multiplicity 0..ceil(N/qty), a catalog of 10-unit offers is exponentially larger than RS-FIX-1, so the < 1 s criterion is not decidable until the generator is defined.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the NFR5 AC defines the generator (offer count, quantity and availability bounds, seed) and includes or drops the p95 clause, and the NFR6 AC includes or drops the log-content scan (which can share the RS-29 scan).

findings.title: PayPal return/cancel handling: token ownership, idempotent authorize, and a session cookie that will not survive the cross-site return
findings.detail: Workflow 4 authorizes when PayPal redirects back to the return URL. The brief does not say that the token must resolve to a payment operation owned by the session's customer. Nor does it say that repeated return hits (refresh, back button) authorize at most once. RS-20 covers capture only. plan.md says Groundwork's session patterns are reused, and Groundwork sets the session cookie with SameSite=Strict (ev:ev-mv16ggcp-011ee455). Browsers do not send Strict cookies on the top-level navigation back from www.sandbox.paypal.com, so the return handler would see no session. The fake adapter page is same-origin, so every deterministic and [B] test would still pass.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the brief or design states four things. (1) The return/cancel handler looks the token up by provider_order_id and checks owner scope (404 otherwise). (2) Authorize is keyed per supplier order and idempotent. (3) The session cookie is SameSite=Lax, or the return handler authenticates by token and then redirects same-site. (4) The fake adapter's approval page is served from a different origin in [B] tests, or the live variant (ARCH-6) covers the return. A repeated-return assertion must be added to RS-18 or RS-20.

findings.title: No runtime spend ceiling or rate limit on customer-triggered paid model calls
findings.detail: NFR6's USD 1 ceiling applies to the live test suite. At runtime, extract and image upload trigger paid model calls with only per-call caps. 'Rate limit' does not occur in the brief (ev:ev-mv16g60f-0190c7f8). A customer looping extract can spend without bound, billed to the user's account (A4).
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the brief adds a configurable daily model budget, after which the provider refuses with a labelled error, plus a per-session rate limit on extract and image upload, each with a deterministic AC.

findings.title: No runtime degraded path when the real model fails; eval corpus location unspecified
findings.detail: The AI feature statement covers test doubles, caps and quality thresholds. It does not say what the customer experiences when the real provider times out or returns schema-invalid output; the fake provider is a test double, not a fallback. The labelled evaluation set (>= 10 requests, >= 6 images) has no stated path or versioning.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the brief states the degraded path: schema_ok = false, all fields unknown, manual entry of every field, journey continues, with a [D] test. The eval corpus must be committed under a named, versioned path.

findings.title: Model rephrasing of planner explanations adds cost and injection surface for no required outcome
findings.detail: ai/explain.js lets the model rephrase planner-trace explanations, and 'never add facts' is not testable as stated. No RS id requires this feature. It adds a second paid call per plan, and catalog text (an RS-05 injection vector) flows into that prompt.
findings.recommendation: Render explanations deterministically from the trace by default. If rephrasing is kept, make it opt-in and labelled, and cover it with the RS-05 control-run comparison and a check that every number in the output appears in the trace.

findings.title: Idempotency details to pin in design
findings.detail: Reusing an Idempotency-Key with a different body should be refused, not replayed. The research says PayPal-Request-Id must be unique per call type and proposes <operationKey>:<kind>. The brief says PayPal-Request-Id = operation key, which is consistent only if each kind has its own row and key.
findings.recommendation: Record both rules in the design's interface contracts.

findings.title: Design-blocking open questions have workable defaults; record them as decisions
findings.detail: Q1, Q3 and Q6 block design, but the brief already states defaults: A2 single-credential fallback, haiku with a USD 1 ceiling, and A10 polling fallback. Q8 is answered by the goal (English interface).
findings.recommendation: Record the defaults as decisions so design can proceed, and keep Q1/Q3/Q6 open for the user to override.

findings.title: Risk register misses three material risks
findings.detail: Three material risks have no entry. (1) An authorization can expire or pass its honour window while the saga waits for supplier confirmations; the validity periods are unverified (ev:ev-mv16gcdz-01d03c53). (2) Browser installation on judges' clean clones (ARCH-5). (3) node:sqlite is still experimental: it emits an ExperimentalWarning on 22.22 (ev:ev-mv16fndw-01e46e13) and is flagged before 22.13.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the register adds these three risks with likelihood, impact, mitigation and owner. For authorization expiry, the mitigation should re-read expiration_time and void and re-authorize.

findings.title: Upload validation basis and ownership unspecified
findings.detail: RS-39 rejects non-PNG/JPEG/WebP files but does not say whether by declared content type or by file signature, so a declared image/png with arbitrary bytes might pass. The AC also does not assert that only the owning customer can attach an image to a request; RS-27 covers reads only.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when RS-39 specifies magic-byte detection and an owner check, each with an assertion.

findings.title: Credential-per-merchant is unverified, and its single-credential fallback weakens live RS-22
findings.detail: A2 is reasonable but rests on search summaries marked 'verify' (ev:ev-mv16gcdz-01d03c53). I could not check paypal.com either; it is blocked here. A2 implies one buyer approval per supplier order, which the UI must announce before the journey starts. In single-credential mode, the refund of supplier 1 and the capture of supplier 2 hit the same account, so live RS-22 no longer demonstrates cross-merchant compensation.
findings.recommendation: State in A2 that the number of buyer approvals equals the number of supplier orders and is shown up front. Name the RS-18..26 live rows that single-credential mode weakens and label them in the evidence table.

findings.title: Core architecture and the canonical fixture live outside the submission
findings.detail: The Architecture section says 'Modules, data model, contracts, planner and saga are as specified in docs/build/plan.md section 2-6 and are adopted unchanged here'. The RS-FIX-1 table (prices, fees, ready times, compatibility) is not in the brief either: the brief has 0 supplier table rows and goal.md has 5 (ev:ev-mv16g60f-0190c7f8). The submission pins only brief.md, so an approval would vouch for plan.md and goal.md content that is neither pinned nor reviewable through the gate. Several ACs depend on that content: RS-06..11 on the fixture and the planner multiplicity rule; RS-36 on the state tables; RS-20..22 on the saga order. The engine refuses artifact citations outside the submission, which is why plan.md and goal.md are cited here as file evidence.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the resubmission either includes docs/build/plan.md (and the fixture source) as submitted artifacts, or inlines into the brief the RS-FIX-1 table with inventory (ARCH-1), the planner feasibility and multiplicity rules, the four state machines with the derivation table (ARCH-2), and the saga order with claim and void rules (ARCH-3).

findings.title: RS-14 needs a busy timeout: without it the losing process gets 'database is locked', not OUT_OF_STOCK
findings.detail: The brief claims 'WAL + BEGIN IMMEDIATE + CHECK constraints gives serialisable conditional updates sufficient for RS-14'. My two-process race on node:sqlite (ev:ev-mv16fndw-01e46e13) gave these results. With the default busy timeout of 0: one RESERVED, the other 'ERROR database is locked'. With PRAGMA busy_timeout=3000: one RESERVED, the other OUT_OF_STOCK, final reserved = on_hand = 1. The design is feasible, but the claim is incomplete, and RS-14 as written would fail or flake without the timeout.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the brief states the busy-timeout setting (PRAGMA busy_timeout, which works on 22.5+) and maps SQLITE_BUSY after the timeout to a retryable 503 rather than a 500. RS-14 must assert that the loser receives OUT_OF_STOCK, not a lock error.

findings.title: Retention of images and request PII depends on a manual admin reset and is only partly tested
findings.detail: A5 and RS-39 say images are deleted with the request 'or by admin reset after 7 days'. No automatic job is specified, the 7-day rule has no AC, no workflow or route lets a customer delete a request, and the retention of raw_text, extractions and account data is not stated.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the brief specifies an automatic retention sweep (or states that retention is manual-only for the demo and says so in the README), the customer route that deletes a request, and a [D] assertion for the 7-day sweep.

It does not list an operation whose own status is unknown. An operation with a lost authorize response is therefore in none of these lists when supersession, refusal, abandonment or expiry fires. The reconciler later resolves it to authorized, and nothing persists a void intent for it. The provider authorization stays open until it expires. Derivation row 4 then shows cancelling indefinitely, and row 2 never escalates it. My implementation of the 13-row table returns cancelling for this case even after 2000 minutes (ev:ev-mv1b5tno-019d3877, GAP case). Placement correction 2 meant to close this, but its wording ('approved with an authorize call still in intent or unknown') matches only the restart case, where the operation is still approved.
evidence: artifact:.eccode/artifacts/architecture/brief.md#State machines (`domain/states.js`; transitions outside these tables are refused and audited)
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the design (1) extends the void rule to operations in unknown whose last call is authorize, so they are voided once the reconciler resolves them to authorized, and (2) adds a [D] assertion: lost authorize response, then supersession, then reconciliation gives exactly one void call and the operation ends voided. Optionally, row 2 also escalates an authorized operation of a superseded or non_executable version that has had no void intent for longer than the pending limit.

findings.title: RS-20 forbids any provider call by losing executors, but the saga re-reads expiration_time from the provider before the claim
findings.detail: Saga step 1 revalidates 'a provider expiration_time (re-read from the provider just before the claim)'. That read happens before BEGIN IMMEDIATE, so every one of the 10 concurrent execute requests in RS-20 performs it. RS-20 says the nine losers 'return the current state without any provider call'. As written, the implementation must break one of the two statements.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when saga step 1 and RS-20 agree. Either move the expiration re-read after the claim (by the lease holder, before the first capture; failure then runs the void rule) or narrow RS-20 to 'without any capture, void or refund call' and allow the read-only authorization GETs.

findings.title: NFR1's Node 22.5 branch does not reach child processes spawned by the multi-process tests
findings.detail: If the user answers Q9 by keeping 22.5, NFR1 says every npm script and the README start command pass --experimental-sqlite. RS-14, RS-20 and RS-26 spawn separate Node processes. A child spawned with process.execPath does not inherit execArgv; it does inherit NODE_OPTIONS. Checked on Node 22.22.0: the child's execArgv lacked --experimental-sqlite, while NODE_OPTIONS carrying --experimental-sqlite --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning was inherited and accepted (ev:ev-mv1b64bb-01e7637d). On 22.5-22.12 those children could not load node:sqlite. This only matters under the 22.5 answer.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the 22.5 branch of NFR1 sets the flag through NODE_OPTIONS in the npm scripts (or requires spawned test processes to pass process.execArgv), and states that the multi-process tests are part of the 22.5 pass condition.

findings.title: Authentication contract is missing from the self-contained brief; the webhook route conflicts with the CSRF rule
findings.detail: The architecture names 'auth (scrypt, sessions, CSRF, RBAC default-deny, owner scope)' and RS-27/28/30 depend on sessions. The API contracts, however, list no sign-in, sign-out or session routes, no session lifetime or rotation, no account provisioning (customer self sign-up or seeded demo accounts), and no throttling of sign-in attempts. Throttling matters most for the startup-provided admin password on a publicly reachable demo. The trust-boundary text also requires the CSRF header on 'every non-GET route'. That would block POST /api/webhooks/paypal/:merchantKey, which has no session and is authenticated by signature instead.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the design contracts list the auth routes, session TTL and rotation on sign-in, and how customer and supplier accounts are provisioned. They must also add a sign-in rate limit or lockout with a [D] assertion, and state that the webhook route is CSRF-exempt and authenticated by signature only.

findings.title: Saga lease takeover while the first executor is still inside a capture call is not fenced
findings.detail: The lease is 60 s and renewed per step. No PayPal HTTP timeout is stated, and 'intent treated as unknown' is stated only for startup. A reconciler in a second process that takes over an expired lease 'resumes at the first supplier order that is not captured'. That order is still authorized while the first process waits on its capture call. The deterministic UNIQUE key does not stop a re-send of the same provider_calls row, and the brief itself calls the provider-side PayPal-Request-Id only a backstop with unverified retention. Nothing says that late writes by the old executor are conditional on still holding the lease. The likelihood is low, but the impact is a double capture (RISK-3).
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the design states three things. (1) The PayPal call timeout is well below the lease (for example 20 s against 60 s). (2) On any takeover, every capture call in intent is treated as unknown and resolved by reading provider state before any re-send. (3) Saga writes are conditional on executor_id and lease_until (fencing). RS-26 or RS-20 must also gain an assertion: process 1 stalls mid-capture past the lease, process 2 takes over, and the fake provider records exactly one capture per supplier order.

resolvedFindings.resolution: Inventory is pinned at on_hand = 1, reserved = 0 for A-E in the inlined fixture table, loaded by the seed with demo: true. RS-06/09/10/11/14 cite it. RS-06 adds the multiplicity guard (A on_hand 2 gives Ax2 at 7000), and the oracle property test uses on_hand 0-3. Independently confirmed: A1B1E1 is the only one of 27 inventories that satisfies RS-06/09/10/11, and every expected outcome reproduces.

resolvedFindings.resolution: (a) authorization_pending, capture_pending and refund_pending are in the payment table with reconciler polling. Capture never starts from authorization_pending, and handover stays blocked while capture_pending (RS-21, RS-22, RS-25). (b) A 13-row precedence table derives every goal aggregate state, including cancelling, refunding and failed_needs_attention. (c) RS-36 carries four derivation assertions, all reproduced by an independent implementation.

RS-20 uses two OS processes x 5 requests. (2) The reservation is consumed in the same transaction; expiry touches only active rows, and RS-15 asserts that an expiry pass after the claim changes nothing. (3) The void rule covers RS-13/15/17/18/21 and authorization expiry, with buyer next steps and assertions in each AC. (4) Supersession stops once the supplier order is confirmed or the plan is executing, and this is asserted in RS-13. Edge residuals are tracked as minors ARCH-22, ARCH-23 and ARCH-26.

RS-34 and its AC cover fake adapters (simulated: true, badge, banner), the Sandbox adapter (provider: paypal-sandbox, sandbox: true, 'PayPal Sandbox - no real money'), seeded demo data (demo: true, 'Demo data' badge) and the 'Test prices, not market prices' notice. They are tested [D; B] for both adapters, and config refuses non-Sandbox hosts.

(a) The brief adopts Node >= 22.13 as a narrowing pending the user's answer Q9 and keeps a 22.5 pass condition (--experimental-sqlite in every script). The busy timeout is set by PRAGMA, which works from 22.5; I confirmed PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000 reads back 5000. (b) The script layout is npm test (offline node --test, launches no browser), npm run test:browser (Playwright, one-time browser install in the README), test:live-model and test:live-paypal. Every [B] AC names test:browser. A residual for the 22.5 branch is tracked as minor ARCH-24.

RS-31 and RS-32 each have (a) a deterministic [B] fake-adapter variant with the approval page on a different site and (b) a user-run [LP browser] variant through the hosted Sandbox approval page, marked Unverified with blocker A6/Q2. Success Criteria require the demo video to show the Sandbox approval page.

The brief now inlines the RS-FIX-1 table with inventory, the planner rules (multiplicity bound, feasibility, objective, codes, relaxations), four state machines, the derivation table, the saga with claim and void rules, the data model and the API contracts. It declares itself authoritative over plan.md, and the phrase 'adopted unchanged' no longer occurs.

Relaxations are computed by re-solving with one constraint removed. RS-10 asserts budget 9500 gives A+E and deadline 11:20 gives D at 8000, and that no max-pickups relaxation appears. Reproduced independently.

The NFR5 AC defines the generator (seeds 1-200, 12 offers, bounds) and keeps p95 with a measurement rule. The NFR6 AC adds the log-content scan and the haiku default.

The return/cancel handlers look up the operation by provider_order_id with an owner check (404 otherwise). Authorize is keyed so:<id>:authorize:1 and idempotent. The cookie is SameSite=Lax. The fake approval page is served from 127.0.0.1 while the app runs on localhost. RS-20 asserts that three repeated returns give one authorize call, and RS-27 asserts the cross-customer token case.

A daily model budget (RS_MODEL_DAILY_BUDGET_USD) and a per-customer rate limit of 10 per 10 minutes, counted in SQLite, are added. NFR6 asserts 503 MODEL_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED on the third call and 429 RATE_LIMITED on the 11th.

Explanations are template-rendered from planner codes. Rephrasing is opt-in (RS_EXPLAIN_REPHRASE=1), labelled, and discarded if it contains a number or supplier code absent from the trace. RS-05 covers it.
A key reused with a different body gets 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED. PayPal-Request-Id is the operation key, which encodes the call kind. Asserted in RS-16.
The defaults are recorded as decision dec-mv16pz0g-01d5c4c2 and cited in Open Questions Q1/Q3/Q4/Q6/Q8, which stay open for the user.

A2 states that the number of approvals equals the number of supplier orders and is shown up front. It names the live rows that single-credential mode weakens (RS-19/20/22/23/24), and the evidence table must label them.

An hourly automatic 7-day image sweep and DELETE /api/requests/:id (409 while money is held, tombstone after settlement) are added. Retention of raw text is stated for the README in A5. RS-39 asserts the sweep with a pinned clock.

findings.title: Reserve idempotency ignores the plan id: a reused key replays another plan's reservation
findings.detail: Interface Contracts > Conventions: the scope is (user id, route template, key) and the body hash is sha256 of the canonical parsed body. For POST /api/plans/:id/reserve the body is always {} and unknown fields are ignored, so a key first used on plan X and then sent to plan Y finds the same (user, '/api/plans/:id/reserve', key, sha256('{}')) row. It replays X's 200/201 response (reservation and orders of X) instead of 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED. reservations.operation_key 'res:<customerId>:<key>' (003_planning.sql) is UNIQUE per customer as well, so plan Y can never be reserved under that key, and the collision's error is unspecified once the key row is purged. The security reviewer reproduced the replay on the spec's DDL: 'reserve plan 9 with the same key: {status:201, replayed:true, ... planVersionId:7}' (ev:ev-mv1cj3km-010da2d1; their SEC-4, rated minor there). I rate it major because RS-16 requires that reusing a key for a different request change nothing and return 422, and the contract is frozen for parallel implementers. The SPA stores keys per planVersionId, which hides the defect in the UI but not in the API.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the request fingerprint includes the concrete path (or the plan id) as well as the body: either the scope is (user, method + concrete path, key) or the hash covers {planId, body}, and operation_key includes the plan id. The spec must also state the error for an operation-key collision. Add a [D] case to reserve-idempotency.test.js: the same key on a second plan returns 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED with no reservation, ledger or order rows.

findings.title: Rescue-status derivation is not total: superseded plan awaiting its replan matches no row
findings.detail: P is 'the newest version that is not superseded'. After supersession (Supersession > Effect and Replan), the only version is superseded until the replan stores a new one. Storing it checks offers_hash with up to 3 retries and has no defined outcome once the retries run out. The queue may also wait for the next reconciler tick after a crash. In that state rows 1-4 do not match once the voids are done. Row 5 needs an infeasible latest run, rows 6-12 need P, and row 13 needs no planning run. My derivation probe implements the brief's 13 rows, the spec's ARCH-22 clause and the OQ-D2 row. It confirms RS-36 (i)-(iv) and reports scenario S13 as '<NO ROW MATCHES>' (ev:ev-mv1ciqrf-016a0687). The same probe shows the brief's rows alone also leave OQ-D2's case unmatched, which the spec already patches. deriveRescueStatus's contract returns rule 1..13 with no fallback. GET /api/requests/:id therefore has no defined status in a state RS-32's journey passes through while the SPA polls every 2 s.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the spec defines a total derivation. Add an explicit row, or a definition of P, for 'no current version, replan queued or retries exhausted', with a status from the goal's set or a stated extension and a nextStep (for example WAIT, or REPLAN after the retries run out). Define what happens when the 3 offers_hash retries run out (re-queue or store infeasible). Add a derive.test.js property test: every combination of plan, reservation, operation and fulfilment states reachable through domain/states.js maps to exactly one row and never to undefined.

findings.title: Queued authorize intents have no sender after a crash or a retryable answer; the operation is stranded in 'approved'
findings.detail: The return handler commits 'created -> approved' and queues so:<id>:authorize:1 (started_at NULL) in one transaction. It then runs the call protocol in a later transaction. If the process dies between the two, the call stays queued. Stale-intent recovery matches only 'started_at <= now - 2 x timeout', so it never matches. Reconciler step 6 sends only 'queued void, refund and capture intents'. A repeated return hit answers 303 with no call because the status is no longer 'created'. A 'retryable' answer (401/403/429) also puts the call back to queued. Recovery says it is 're-queued with back-off ... then every tick', but no reconciler step sends authorize. SEC-6 shows that an anonymous webhook flood can induce PayPal 429s on a merchant credential. Consequences: execute returns AUTHORIZATION_PENDING indefinitely. When the void rule fires (expiry, abandon), an 'approved' operation with an authorize call in intent is left 'for later', but nothing resolves it. Row 4 then reports 'cancelling' forever, and row 2 never escalates 'approved' (the probe lists 'approved' among the states that never escalate, scenario S18, ev:ev-mv1ciqrf-016a0687). DELETE /api/requests/:id is refused (PAYMENT_IN_PROGRESS) and admin reset is blocked unless forced.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when, for every call kind, the spec names the component that sends a queued (started_at NULL) or retryable call and when it does so. For authorize, either the reconciler sends it (it is provably unsent), or, if cancel_requested_at is set, the call becomes 'cancelled' and the operation is voided locally. Row 2 must also escalate an operation left in 'approved' with an outstanding authorize call past the unknown limit. Add a [D] test: a fault hook stops the process after the return-handler commit; after a restart and reconcile, exactly one authorize call has been made, or the call is cancelled and the operation 'voided', and the request leaves 'cancelling'.

findings.title: NFR1: on an older Node, npm start fails with 'bad option' before the version gate can name the required version
findings.detail: Deployment: npm start is 'node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning src/index.js'. In the 22.5 branch, every script also gets '--experimental-sqlite' right after 'node'. Node parses these flags before src/index.js runs. My check ran both command shapes on the older Node binaries on this host (ev:ev-mv1cir59-01e77df9). On v20.20.0 and v21.7.3 the 22.5-branch command exits 9 with 'bad option: --experimental-sqlite' and does not name the required version. The >=22.13-branch command does reach the gate there. However, the Node 20 changelog shows --disable-warning was introduced in 20.11.0, so Node 18 and Node 20.0-20.10 fail the default command the same way. npm only warns on engines. The planned test (test/unit/config/node-version.test.js) unit-tests the gate function on this host's Node 22.22, so it cannot see the defect. NFR1 requires that 'on an older Node npm start exits non-zero with a message naming the required version'.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the start path runs the version gate before any version-specific node flag is parsed. For example: 'start' runs a flag-free 'node scripts/check-node.js' first, or src/index.js re-spawns itself with the flags after the check, or the warning is filtered in code instead of by flag. The same applies to the 22.5 branch. Add a [D] or inspection test that runs the actual npm start command line on an older Node binary when one is available (this host has /opt/node20 and /opt/node21), or at least asserts that the start script begins with a flag-free gate.

findings.title: Anyone can lock any known account (admin included) out of sign-in
findings.detail: Folded in from the security reviewer (.eccode/reviews/drafts/design-security-1.md, SEC-1); I also confirmed it from the spec text. Authentication > Throttle refuses a sign-in 'when the username has >= 5 failures in the last 15 min ... before the password is checked, so the correct password is also refused', and T8 asserts that behaviour. The seed publishes fixed usernames (admin, supplier-a..e, cafe1, cafe2). The security reviewer's executable model printed 'attacker (1 IP, 5 requests): 401 x5 | real admin, other IP, correct password: 429 RATE_LIMITED | after the next 5-guess cycle: 429' (ev:ev-mv1cj3km-010da2d1; spec text quoted in ev:ev-mv1chwnv-0109783d H2). Locking out the suppliers stalls confirmations, so reservations expire and the void rule fires. A live demo can be stalled with 40 requests per 15 minutes.
findings.recommendation: Resolved as the security reviewer states. The hard refusal is keyed on (username, IP) with a per-IP global limit. Across IPs a username gets a progressive delay, or a higher threshold that still checks the password. Failures for unknown usernames are counted the same way, so 429-versus-401 does not enumerate accounts. Username keys are normalised (SEC-9). T8 changes to: '6th attempt from the same IP gives 429; the correct password from another IP gives 200'.

findings.title: One customer can hold every supplier's stock, repeatedly, without paying
findings.detail: Folded in from the security reviewer (SEC-2), and consistent with my reading of Reservation and Authentication > Provisioning. Self-registration is on by default (OQ-D3). Requests can be confirmed manually, which needs no model budget. Seeded on_hand is 1 per supplier, and nothing caps live reservations per customer. One customer can therefore reserve every bundle with fresh Idempotency-Keys and repeat after each 30-minute TTL, while every other customer's reserve fails OUT_OF_STOCK and their plans go non_executable. Reproduced on the spec's DDL: 'attacker reserves each supplier bundle: 201 x5 | live reservations held: 5 | victim reserve: 409 OUT_OF_STOCK' (ev:ev-mv1cj3km-010da2d1; spec text in ev:ev-mv1chwnv-0109783d H6).
findings.recommendation: Resolved as the security reviewer states. Add a per-customer cap on live reservations (default 1, for example RS_MAX_LIVE_RESERVATIONS_PER_CUSTOMER), refused with a catalogued 409 or 429 code, and a per-customer daily limit on request creation. Assert both in an API test. Optionally, shorten the TTL until the first PayPal approval.

findings.title: A loopback PayPal stub under npm start is labelled 'PayPal Sandbox', not 'Simulated' (RS-34)
findings.detail: Folded in from the security reviewer (SEC-3). T18 and the wire mapping accept RS_PAYPAL_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port> and a loopback approval host for the paypal-sandbox adapter, with no restriction to tests. Under npm start that produces provider 'paypal-sandbox', simulated:false and sandbox:true, the 'PayPal Sandbox — no real money' badge and no Simulated banner, for a flow that is simulated. RS-34 requires everything that is not real to be labelled. The labelling test asserts the Sandbox labels against this stub. Evidence: spec text quoted in ev:ev-mv1chwnv-0109783d (H5).
findings.recommendation: Resolved when a loopback PayPal base URL and approval host are accepted only under RS_TEST_OFFLINE=1 or RS_TEST_HOOKS=1, and npm start refuses them at startup. The alternative is that loopback mode is labelled simulated:true and sandbox:false, shows the Simulated banner and uses a distinct badge. Either way, add a config test and a labelling test for each case.

findings.title: OQ-D2 default labels a partially refunded executed plan 'cancelled'
findings.detail: With admin refund_order on one supplier's order of an executed plan and the other order collected, the OQ-D2 row returns 'cancelled' (probe S15, ev:ev-mv1ciqrf-016a0687). The buyer did receive and pay for part of the plan, so the aggregate misstates it. A related transient case: reserve losing the race gives 'cancelled' until the replan lands (S20).
findings.recommendation: Resolved when OQ-D2's row gives a state that does not claim the whole purchase was cancelled. For example, keep 'collected' or 'purchase_confirmed' with a message naming the refunded order, or use an explicitly named extension. The derive test should assert it.

findings.title: A void rejected because the authorization was captured is recorded as void_failed while money is captured
findings.detail: Void rule step 6: 'rejected -> read the authorization: VOIDED -> voided, else keep authorized with void_failed = 1'. If the read shows CAPTURED (a late capture from a fenced or stalled sender landed after a read showed none; see SEC-18), the operation still says 'authorized' although the buyer was charged. refund_order only accepts 'captured' under an 'executed' plan, so no tool can refund it. The derivation escalates it (row 2), so it is not silent, but it is stranded.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when a void-result read that shows CAPTURED moves the operation to 'captured' and the compensating-plan refund hook queues so:<id>:refund:1, with a fake-adapter test (capture applied after the void intent).

findings.title: Saga step 3 behaviour for an operation in capture_pending or unknown after takeover is not stated
findings.detail: A pause sets lease_until = now, so reconciler step 5 takes the plan over on every tick (the epoch grows) and resumes 'for the first operation not captured'. That operation is the capture_pending or unknown one. The start CAS refuses (the call is not a fresh intent), so nothing is double-sent, but the spec does not say that step 3 must re-pause without sending, nor that takeover should skip plans whose only open item is pending or unknown.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when step 3 states that an operation in capture_pending or unknown pauses the saga without a send, and the reconciler takes over a paused plan only once that operation is resolved. RS-22's PENDING case should assert that the epoch does not grow per tick.

findings.title: RS-20 test attributes provider calls by pid, which cannot see losers in the winner's process
findings.detail: rs20-two-process-execute asserts 'zero provider calls attributed to the losers' pids'. Four of the nine losers run in the winner's process, so a stray call from one of them would be counted as the winner's.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the test also asserts the exact total of fake_paypal_calls for the run: N getAuthorization reads plus N captures, and nothing else.

findings.title: Traceability gaps: RS-36 lacks its [I] inspection; RS-03's [D] ambiguous-image half names no test
findings.detail: The traceability check (ev:ev-mv1cik0q-01d57f54) finds all 45 ids exactly once, each with a section and a test. It warns that RS-36's row omits the brief's [I] tag. RS-03's row lists degraded-path faults for [D] but not the ambiguous-image assertion, which test/eval/extraction-fake.test.js would cover.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the RS-36 row names its inspection and the RS-03 row names the [D] ambiguous-image test.

findings.title: Per-customer rate limit check and insert are not stated to be atomic across processes
findings.detail: Runtime controls step 1 counts rate_events and then inserts, but only the budget step says 'in one transaction'. Two processes can each count 9 and both insert.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the rate check and insert run in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction, as the budget step does.

findings.title: Compensated plans leave supplier orders 'confirmed'
findings.detail: Fulfilment allows -> cancelled only before the claim, so after CAPTURE_FAILED or post-claim AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED the orders stay 'confirmed' and the supplier dashboard still shows a live order.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the supplier and customer views derive a 'cancelled (payment failed)' presentation for orders of a non_executable plan, or the fulfilment machine adds the edge (a brief change to raise with the orchestrator).

findings.title: Model spend stored as REAL dollars
findings.detail: model_spend.reserved_usd and actual_usd are REAL, and the budget check compares float sums against the budget. Near the boundary the result depends on rounding.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when spend is stored as INTEGER micro-dollars (or the comparison is stated with a fixed rounding), with the NFR6 boundary case asserted.

findings.title: Wire schema acceptance by the CLI --json-schema and the API is verified only at the first live run
findings.detail: I confirmed that every pinned flag exists (ev:ev-mv1cirha-01fe9dfc) and re-ran the designer's stream-json constraint probe (ev:ev-mv1citom-01b59d5c). Whether $defs/$ref and anyOf-with-null schemas are accepted is not exercised offline, and a rejection would send every live extraction to the degraded path.
findings.recommendation: Make schema acceptance an explicit assertion of the cli-image-smoke case and of the first API run, and have the live report record it.

findings.title: Fake approval page CSP form-action 'self' blocks the approve/cancel redirect to the app: [B] payment journeys cannot complete
findings.detail:
Revision 2 adds a contract for the fake approval listener (SEC-12). GET /fake-paypal/checkout/:id is served with CSP "default-src 'none'; style-src 'self'; form-action 'self'", and the listener 'applies the same security headers ... as the app', whose CSP also ends in form-action 'self'. POST .../approve answers 303 to the stored return_url on http://localhost:<port> (the app), and POST .../cancel answers 303 to the cancel_url. Chromium enforces form-action across the redirect chain of a form submission. I reproduced the spec's page with Playwright's Chromium (ev:ev-mv1dhs2e-012e67d4):
- (A) the spec's CSP: the browser stays on the fake page with 'Refused to send form data ... violates the following Content Security Policy directive', and the return route is never hit.
- (B) form-action 'self' plus the app origin: the browser reaches the return route with the SameSite=Lax session cookie.
- (C) no CSP: same as (B).
- (D) control: a Strict cookie is not sent, so the return really is cross-site, which is what RS-31 requires.
As specified, test/browser/journey-happy (RS-31(a)), journey-replacement (RS-32(a)) and the NFR2 keyboard-only happy path cannot get past the first PayPal approval.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when every Content-Security-Policy header the fake approval listener sends either lists the app's return origin in form-action (form-action 'self' <RS_PUBLIC_URL origin>) or omits form-action. That includes the inherited app security headers, because two CSP headers are both enforced. The same applies to the test helper paypal-stub's approval page. Test: a [B] assertion in journey-happy that the approve and cancel clicks land on /api/paypal/return and /api/paypal/cancel with the session (it would have caught this), plus a [D] header test that pins the listener's CSP value.

findings.title: Per-day request limit and live-reservation cap are not reconciled with the browser suites and the user-run demo
findings.detail: RS_MAX_REQUESTS_PER_CUSTOMER_PER_DAY defaults to 10, and request_create events survive request deletion. The [B] files reuse the seeded customers (cafe1/cafe2) for several journeys: happy at 360 and 1280, the keyboard variant, the a11y states, labelling for both adapters and six-questions. The spec does not say whether each [B] file gets a fresh database (server-proc does use a temp RS_DB_PATH) or whether the limit is raised for tests. The user-run Sandbox journeys and demo-video retakes with one account can also hit 10 per day. With a cap of 1 live reservation, an abandoned journey blocks the next one for up to 30 minutes unless 'Abandon purchase' is used.
findings.recommendation: State that every [B] test file starts its own server on a fresh database (or sets the two limits through the environment in test mode). Add a README runbook line for demo operators: raise or reset the limits, use separate accounts, or abandon before retaking.

findings.title: OQ-D6 and OQ-D7: record the status-set extension; the share default could be on
findings.detail: OQ-D6: 'replanning' is a reasonable, honest extension; my probe confirms RS-36 (i)-(iv) are unchanged with it (ev:ev-mv1dkn6p-01cfa3c8). Because it adds to the user's status vocabulary, it belongs in the decision record and in the brief-deviation list the user sees. OQ-D7: the stated reason for keeping the per-customer share off is that 0.2 would refuse NFR6's first two calls. But NFR6's test can pin RS_MODEL_CUSTOMER_DAILY_SHARE=1 in its own environment; with the production defaults (budget 1.00, cap 0.05), a share of 0.2 allows 4 cap-sized reservations per customer. Deferring to the user (Q10) is acceptable.
findings.recommendation: Record OQ-D6 as a decision (eccode decision add). When the user answers Q10, consider defaulting the share to 0.2 with the NFR6 test pinning 1.

resolvedFindings.resolution: Scope (user, key) with a fingerprint over method, concrete path and body; reservations.idempotency_key UNIQUE per customer; operation_key carries the plan id; collisions mapped explicitly; [D] cases include the second plan before and after purge. On the revised DDL the same customer's key on plan 2 is refused by UNIQUE (customer_id, idempotency_key) with no idempotency_keys row present, another customer may reuse the text, and the key PK refuses a second fingerprint.

The derivation is total: row 4a (replanning) for a queued re-plan, a re-plan queue that never drops entries after the retries run out, and a defensive row 14 with a property test. My own implementation of the revised table gives S13/S13b 'replanning', S15 'collected', S15b 'cancelled', S15c (admin refund unknown) 'refunding', and RS-36 (i)-(iv) unchanged. Exhaustive enumeration of 493,074 abstract states reaches row 14 only in 326 unreachable states: a feasible run with no version, or an unknown whose prev_status cannot occur under P's status.

The Sender table names who sends each queued or retryable call kind. A queued authorize is sent by reconciler step 6, or cancelled with the operation voided locally once cancellation is requested. Row 2(a) escalates 'approved' with an outstanding authorize after the unknown limit, and the return-crash integration test covers it. In my derivation probe, S18 ends 'cancelled' (not stuck in cancelling), while S18b (started authorize unknown, 20 min) and S18c (429 re-queued, 20 min) reach failed_needs_attention.

Every flagged script begins with the flag-free 'node scripts/check-node.cjs &&'. I ran the spec's start line verbatim through /bin/sh and through 'npm run start'. On Node 20.20 and 21.7 it exits 1 with 'RescueStock needs Node >= 22.13 (found ...)', and the 22.5-branch line names 22.5. On 22.22 the app starts. Every flagged script in the block carries the gate prefix.

The hard 429 is keyed on (normalised username, IP), 5 per 15 min, plus 20 per IP. Across IPs a username gets only a 1-10 s delay, and the password is still checked. Unknown usernames are counted alike, and T8 is rewritten. On the revised login_failures schema, five failures from the attacker IP reach the pair limit for that IP only: the pair on another IP is 0 and the cross-IP total stays below the delay threshold.

There is a live-reservation cap (default 1) checked inside the reserve BEGIN IMMEDIATE, giving 409 RESERVATION_LIMIT, and 10 requests per customer per day with count and insert atomic, both asserted in abuse-limits.test.js. Two OS processes reserving two different plans for the same customer give exactly RESERVED + RESERVATION_LIMIT. The RS-32 sequence (void-rule release, then replacement reserve) passes under the cap.

Loopback PayPal and Anthropic base URLs, and a loopback approval host, are accepted only with RS_TEST_OFFLINE=1, which sets labels.testMode and shows the 'Test mode — local stubs, nothing is real' banner. Startup refuses them otherwise, and T18 and the RS-34 traceability name the config and labelling tests for both cases. This is a text-level fix, checked against the spec's Conventions, Security and Deployment sections and the traceability run.

findings.title: Fresh customer per browser journey vs the 5-registrations-per-IP-per-hour limit
findings.detail: The F-TR-15 fix has every [B] journey register a fresh customer through POST /api/auth/register. All of them come from 127.0.0.1, and registration is limited to 5 per IP per hour. That limit is not configurable and the harness does not raise it. The harness raises only the daily request limit. Each file has a fresh database, but a file with more than five journeys will get 429 register_ip on the sixth registration. a11y-states covers seven states at two widths, and journey-happy covers 360, 1280, the keyboard-only run and the cancel path.

findings.detail: With the production default share of 0.2 (revision 3), NFR6's stated configuration refuses the first extract with scope 'customer' (my gate model, ev:ev-mv1dzog2-017e0120). That configuration is a fake cap of 0.10 and a budget of 0.25, under which the AC says 'the third extract is refused'. The spec pins RS_MODEL_CUSTOMER_DAILY_SHARE=1 for the NFR6 case and states why, so the design is consistent. However, a reader who checks NFR6 literally, with the brief's settings and the defaults, sees a different outcome.

resolvedFindings.resolution: The fake approval listener and the paypal-stub approval page now send exactly one CSP, approvalPageCsp(appOrigin) = default-src 'none'; style-src 'self'; form-action 'self' <appOrigin>; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none', and no longer inherit the app CSP. I read both strings from the final spec and ran them in Chromium 141. Approve lands on /api/paypal/return and Cancel on /api/paypal/cancel, each with the SameSite=Lax session and no CSP console error. Adding the app CSP as a second header makes Chromium refuse the submission. The spec adds the [B] round-trip assertion (journey-happy, journey-replacement, keyboard-only run) and a [D] test pinning the single header.

Every [B] file starts its own server on a fresh seeded database, and each journey uses a fresh customer. The harnesses raise the daily request limit and keep the live-reservation cap at 1. The README has an operator note for retakes, and the admin reset clears request_create rate events. I checked that deleting those rows is permitted while the append-only ledgers still refuse DELETE. A new consequence of this fix, the register-per-IP limit, is tracked as F-TR-17 (minor).

OQ-D6 and OQ-D7 are in a 'Decisions requested' table for the orchestrator and the user. The share now defaults to 0.2 in production (read from the spec env table), and the NFR6 case pins 1. My gate model confirms that with the defaults one customer's 5th cap-sized call is refused with scope customer while another customer's call succeeds, and that NFR6's configuration with the share pinned gives ok, ok, refused (global).

review.summary:
Review of plan submission sub-mv1eqk2q-01cc29a2 (plan.json 92e23914..., plan.md 9199cc75...), against the approved brief and design revision 3.
What holds, from checks I ran myself:
- `plan validate` is clean (ev:ev-mv1exo5j-01eb88f8).
- Structure: all 29 tasks carry an owner, dependencies, inputs, outputs, files, acceptance criteria and a verification command with cwd '.' (ev:ev-mv1exmy0-01d4615b).
- Dependency graph: no cycle and no dependency on a later phase.
- Concurrency: all 19 concurrent pairs have disjoint ownership; the shared wiring files (src/app.js, src/main.js, src/routes/plans.js, package.json) are only ever owned by serialized tasks; no glob reaches .eccode/, .claude/ or hooks.
- Coverage: all 45 ids are claimed by exactly one phase, and every one of the 59 [D]/[B] test files the design's traceability names is owned in or before its claiming phase and run by a verification command in that phase.
- The criterion moves (RS-15 and RS-38 to F, RS-04 to E, RS-34, NFR3 and NFR5 to G, RS-36 to C) follow real dependencies.
- The live checks are kept outside the tasks and marked Unverified.
- The lesson decision is evidence-backed (ev:ev-mv1eya53-01fe0832).
The problem: on Node 22.22, a node --test command whose globs match nothing exits 0 with 0 tests (ev:ev-mv1exnz5-01303ad6). 11 of the 29 verification commands therefore pass before their task's work exists: b1 and b2 use globs only, the frontend tasks d4, e5, f3 and g1 rerun files that exist from c5, and the test-engineer tasks c6, d5, e6, f4 and g3 run only `npm test && npm run test:browser`. b2 is the task that proves RS-06..RS-11. Changes requested for that one major finding (F-PL-1).
The schedule risk (about 400-600 minutes of work against about 300 left) is recorded as F-PL-2 for the user's decision. It is not a reason to reject.

findings.title: 11 of 29 verification commands pass before the task's work exists
findings.detail:
On Node 22.22, `node --test` with a glob that matches nothing exits 0 with '# tests 0'. A missing explicit file or a missing --import module exits 1 (ev:ev-mv1exnz5-01303ad6). For each command, my plan check looked for a referenced file that the task itself creates first (ev:ev-mv1exmy0-01d4615b). These have none:
- b1-foundation-core and b2-domain: globs only. b2 proves RS-06..RS-11 and the derivation totality.
- d4, e5, f3, g1: the same command as c5, `node --test test/scan/frontend.test.js "test/unit/frontend/**/*.test.js"`, whose files exist from c5.
- c6, d5, e6, f4, g3: `npm test && npm run test:browser`, which are glob-based scripts. Before the task's integration and browser files exist, these pass on whatever exists.
The plan gate requires each verification to fail before the work and pass after. The phase reviewers must rerun exactly these commands, so a green run would not show that the task's own tests exist or pass.
findings.recommendation:
Resolved when every task's command names at least one test file that the task itself creates, so my plan check reports 0 pre-passing tasks. Examples:
- b1: test/unit/config/hosts.test.js, test/unit/db/migrate.test.js.
- b2: test/unit/domain/planner-fixture.test.js, planner-oracle.property.test.js, derive.test.js, states.test.js, test/timing/planner-generator.test.js.
- The frontend tasks: a per-phase file such as test/unit/frontend/extraction.test.js, payments.test.js, recovery.test.js, a11y-labels.test.js.
- The test-engineer tasks: keep `npm test` and append their own files explicitly, e.g. `npm test && npm run test:browser -- test/browser/journey-infeasible.test.js && node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning --import ./test/helpers/net-guard.js --test test/integration/rs14-two-process-reserve.test.js test/integration/rs14-db-busy.test.js`.

findings.title: The schedule likely exceeds the remaining runtime budget
findings.detail: status reports 177/480 minutes used, so about 300 remain. The plan's own estimate is 400-600 minutes (29 implementer dispatches, a 20-dispatch critical path, 6 phase reviews, maxConcurrency 2). The plan is close to minimal under one owner per task. The only same-owner, serial merge that does not lengthen the critical path is g3 + g4 (both test-engineer), which saves one dispatch. Other merges would mix owners or serialize concurrent work (e3/e4, d2/d3, f1/f2). The plan already routes the choice to the user (limits.raise or a descoping order). Waiting until the end of phase C risks stopping mid-phase with half-built money paths.
